forecaster_note: Thu: more SW'ly morning wind so there'll be cleaner options in the S corners; size is overhead across the south-facing beaches and messy with the onshores later. Fri: a low in the Tasman sends better-quality SE swell, well overhead on open beaches; light westerlies keep it clean until a mid-arvo onshore switch — aim for the AM high. Sat: swell eases slowly, NNW/NW winds add texture to exposed breaks. — Surfline forecaster (Thu 8 Oct)

wind.summary: SSW 13 kph (gust 20) at 6am, swinging SW/offshore-ish ~15 kph at 9am, then S/SE onshore ~19 kph by 3pm. Fri AM light W (~7 kph).

shark.summary: Northern Beaches, last 24h: tagged White Shark #2285 pinged the Palm Beach receiver 5 times between 5:07am and 6:05am today (newest ~10 min ago) — it's actively hanging around the northern end. Nothing at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the last 24h (last Manly/North Steyne detection was White Shark #2880 at 5:06pm Tue, ~37h ago). Feed is current (~28 real detections statewide in 24h). Check the live map before paddling out, especially dawn at the northern beaches.

days.note: Swell's eased to 8ft @ 10s but still dead-S, with a lighter SW wind cleaning the S corners early. Manly/the corners are the pick if you want a surf; Dee Why wraps poorly. Friday's SE swell is the main event.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Better-quality SE swell arrives off a Tasman low — well overhead on the open beaches, light W until mid-arvo, then NE onshore. Pick of the week: aim for the 8:03am high.

dee-why.window: W 6–7 kph to ~9am, NE onshore ~15 kph from midday. High 8:03am (1.5m), low 2:07pm. SE swell wraps far better than the S — Point rights should be on.

long-reef.window: W offshore am, NE onshore from noon. Big and open — high tide helps; head to the Point/south end for shape.

curl-curl.window: W offshore am; sizey on the open beach — the south corner is the smaller option. High 8:03am.

manly.window: W offshore am, tide 8:03am high. Most protected of the four — good bet if open beaches are too big.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Low-confidence: swell eases slowly into Sat with NNW/NW wind adding texture — S-facing zones pick up the best sets at dawn on the early high (8:41am). Sun is small with mixed NE/S wind swells; recheck Fri. Friday's still the pick.

dee-why.window: Sat: NNW 6–9 kph am, easing swell; Point rights wrap better than this week. Aim for the 8:41am high. Sun small (2–3ft), wind uncertain.

long-reef.window: Sat: NNW offshore am — the South end picks up a couple of good sets at dawn. Sun small.

curl-curl.window: Sat: NNW offshore am, early high is the go. Sun unknown — recheck.

manly.window: Sat: NNW offshore am, easing swell. Sun small and mixed.
